name: route-timetable
title: Route timetable
description: A line's timetable as a real table: stops down the side, trips across, the next departure marked in words, and on a phone a stop picker with that stop's times.
docs: Pass stops ({ id, name, note }) in route order and trips ({ id, label, note, times }), where times is an object of 24-hour clock times by stop id: { harbour: "08:00", marina: "08:12" }. A stop that is left out, or null, is one the trip does not stop at: the cell shows a dash and says 'does not stop'. now decides which trip is next and which have gone; leave it out to use the browser's clock (read after the page is live, then every half minute) or pass it to get the same page on the server and in tests. Times are read in timeZone (default UTC) and written in locale (default en-US, so '7:42 AM'; en-GB writes '07:42'). The reader picks their stop in the picker above the grid: pass highlightStop with onHighlightStopChange to control it, or defaultHighlightStop to start somewhere. The next trip at that stop is marked 'Next', trips that have left it are muted, and a line says how long to wait. The grid opens scrolled to the next trip and follows when another stop is picked, but never moves by itself as time passes. The stop column stays pinned and the scroll box takes the keyboard. In a box narrower than 36rem the grid is replaced by the picker and the list of that stop's times, with the caption above the picker. There everything before the last trip that left folds into one line to open: that trip stays, as context, and a run that skips the stop is folded with the rest. caption names the table, note goes under it, and labels translates every word, including the line shown when there are no stops or trips.
